tour.overview:
Before reaching the sea, the Mekong, after 4,350 kilometres from the Tibetan plateau, divides into nine branches, which the Vietnamese call Cuu Long, the Nine Dragons. Its delta is a flat, green world of rice fields, fruit orchards, coconut groves and canals, where boats are still the main way to travel and markets float on the water. Ben Tre, an island province between branches of the river, is known as the land of coconuts.

This private day from Saigon shows the delta's river life with a licensed guide and a car. You cross the Mekong in your own boat, glide through narrow canals in a sampan, visit family workshops, cycle between orchards, listen to southern folk music and have lunch in a garden.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Ho Chi Minh City
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, private boat, sampan and bicycles
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Mekong river by private boat.
• The water-coconut canals of Ben Tre by sampan.
• Coconut candy and rice-paper workshops.
• Orchards and villages by bicycle.
• A garden lunch and folk music.

WHY THIS WORKS
We use a private boat and choose smaller canals and family workshops instead of the busy stops of the group tours.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, nature lovers and anyone who wants to see rural Vietnam.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To see a true floating market at dawn, choose a two-day trip with a night in Can Tho for the Cai Rang market.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about two hours each way. The delta is hot and humid; boats have shade. The famous floating markets are farther, in Can Tho and Cai Rang, and best seen at dawn on an overnight trip.

days.name: A private boat on the Mekong, sampan canals, workshops, cycling, folk music and a garden lunch in Ben Tre
days.description:
What to expect: the river life of the Mekong Delta with a licensed guide, private car, boats, bicycles and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drive south, about two hours, across the flat delta to the Mekong at My Tho. Your private boat carries you across the wide brown river, past dredgers, fishing boats and islands named after the dragon, unicorn, turtle and phoenix, to the canals of Ben Tre.

You visit family workshops along the water: one where coconut flesh is pressed and boiled with malt into chewy coconut candy, another where rice paper and rice popped in hot sand are made by hand. You then change to a sampan, paddled by a local woman in a conical hat, and glide through narrow canals shaded by water-coconut palms, whose fronds meet overhead.

You cycle along quiet concrete lanes between orchards of longan, rambutan, pomelo and mango, past houses with family altars and ancestors' graves in the gardens. At a family home you taste seasonal fruit and honey tea with kumquat, while local musicians play don ca tai tu, southern Vietnamese chamber music, recognised by UNESCO as intangible heritage. Lunch is in a garden restaurant, with elephant-ear fish, fried crisp and wrapped at the table with herbs and rice paper, and other delta dishes. Your boat takes you back across the river, and you are back in Saigon at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:30 – Private boat across the Mekong.
10:00 – Coconut candy and rice-paper workshops.
10:45 – Sampan through the coconut canals.
11:30 – Cycling between orchards.
12:15 – Fruit, honey tea and folk music.
13:00 – Garden lunch.
14:30 – Boat back and drive to Saigon.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• For a dawn floating market, choose our two-day version with a night in Can Tho.
• Cycling is gentle and optional.
• The delta is especially green in the rainy season, from May to November.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, private boat and sampan, bicycles, workshop visits, fruit and tea, folk music, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, purchases, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see a floating market?
faq.answer: The large floating markets, Cai Rang and Phong Dien, are near Can Tho and are best at dawn. We recommend a two-day version with a night there.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: Yes, your own boat on the Mekong, and sampans for your group in the canals.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, in a garden restaurant. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the boats, the bicycles and the coconut candy. Child seats and child bikes are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Boarding boats and sampans needs some agility. The cycling can be replaced by a walk or an electric cart.

faq.question: Do we have to cycle?
faq.answer: No. It is gentle and optional; you can walk or ride in a cart instead.

faq.question: Will we be pushed to buy things?
faq.answer: No. You may buy coconut candy at the workshops if you like, but there are no commission stops.

faq.question: Is it hot?
faq.answer: Yes, all year. The boats have shade, and we carry water.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam, especially for the sampan paddlers, but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, sun cream, insect repellent and sandals with straps.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. December to April is dry; the rainy season is lush, with short showers, and the fruit season peaks from May to August.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
